05 · Set association

Load packages

enrichVolcano (not on CRAN) is called with :: for its label cleaner.

pacman::p_load(
  here, limpa, limma, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readr, readxl, writexl
)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/05_set_association/a_script/05_set_association.qmd")

Read inputs

Four inputs: the set catalogue from 00_build_gene_sets, the singscore matrix from 03_run_singscore (one row per set, one column per sample), the sample targets stored with the protein estimates and the per-leg phenotype measurements.

stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "05_set_association")
gene_sets <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
set_catalog <- read_excel(file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"), "set_catalog")
set_score <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "03_run_singscore", "c_data", "set_scores.rds"))
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
targets <- proteins$targets
phenotype <- read_csv(here("00_Input", "phenotype.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(set_score)

Select sets

Only sets the catalogue marks as qualifies are tested. values holds their scores in catalogue order, and collection_sizes counts sets per collection; that count is the denominator for the chance comparison further down.

catalog <- set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  select(set_id, database, pathway, measured_size)
values <- set_score[catalog$set_id, ]
collection_sizes <- count(catalog, database)
collection_sizes

Pair the samples

Every comparison here is paired, so each sample needs its partner. by_timepoint spreads the targets to one row per leg, with the T1 and T2 sample IDs side by side. legs keeps legs sampled at both time points. Treatment comes from the targets, never the leg letter: leg assignment was counterbalanced.

by_timepoint <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  select(leg_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sample_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = sample_id)
legs <- drop_na(by_timepoint, T1, T2) |> arrange(participant, treatment)
head(legs, 4)
# A tibble: 4 × 6
  leg_id participant leg   treatment T1       T2      
  <chr>  <chr>       <chr> <chr>     <chr>    <chr>   
1 S02_R  S02         R     BFR       S02_R_T1 S02_R_T2
2 S02_L  S02         L     HLRT      S02_L_T1 S02_L_T2
3 S03_R  S03         R     BFR       S03_R_T1 S03_R_T2
4 S03_L  S03         L     HLRT      S03_L_T1 S03_L_T2

Widening the legs on treatment gives one row per participant with the BFR and HLRT legs side by side. Participants missing either leg are dropped.

delta_pairs <- legs |>
  select(participant, treatment, leg_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = leg_id) |>
  drop_na(BFR, HLRT)
c(legs = nrow(legs), change = nrow(delta_pairs))
  legs change 
    65     32

The change in each set’s score per leg is T2 minus T1. Its columns are named by leg, so the BFR and HLRT legs of a participant can be picked out with delta_pairs.

delta <- values[, legs$T2] - values[, legs$T1]
colnames(delta) <- legs$leg_id

Prepare the phenotype

Four outcomes, each a post minus pre change in one leg: cross-sectional area (csa) and echo intensity (echo) of vastus lateralis (vl) and rectus femoris (rf). Echo intensity falls as muscle composition improves, so a negative change is the favourable one. The join is declared one-to-one, because a duplicated phenotype row would silently misalign every leg below.

outcomes <- c("vl_csa", "vl_echo", "rf_csa", "rf_echo")
leg_phenotype <- legs |>
  left_join(
    select(phenotype, -treatment),
    by = c("participant", "leg"), relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vl_csa = vl_csa_post_cm2 - vl_csa_pre_cm2,
    vl_echo = vl_echo_post_au - vl_echo_pre_au,
    rf_csa = rf_csa_post_cm2 - rf_csa_pre_cm2,
    rf_echo = rf_echo_post_au - rf_echo_pre_au
  )
head(select(leg_phenotype, leg_id, treatment, all_of(outcomes)), 4)
# A tibble: 4 × 6
  leg_id treatment vl_csa vl_echo rf_csa rf_echo
  <chr>  <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>

The differential analysis works within participant: BFR minus HLRT for the score change and for each outcome change. Participant traits that move both legs cancel out of that difference.

paired <- delta[, delta_pairs$BFR] - delta[, delta_pairs$HLRT]
colnames(paired) <- delta_pairs$participant
paired_outcome <- map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
  value <- set_names(leg_phenotype[[name]], leg_phenotype$leg_id)
  value[delta_pairs$BFR] - value[delta_pairs$HLRT]
})

Correlate each set

Spearman correlation ranks both variables and correlates the ranks, so it measures any monotone relationship and is not pulled by single extreme legs. cor.test() computes its p with algorithm AS 89, which is exact below 10 observations and an Edgeworth series approximation at the 32 and 65 used here. Singscore changes can tie exactly; for those sets cor.test() warns and uses the t approximation instead, and the warnings are suppressed.

spearman_by_row <- function(values, outcome) {
  fits <- suppressWarnings(apply(values, 1, function(row) {
    test <- cor.test(row, outcome, method = "spearman")
    c(r = unname(test$estimate), p = test$p.value)
  }))
  tibble(
    set_id = rownames(values), n = sum(!is.na(outcome)),
    r = unname(fits["r", ]), p = unname(fits["p", ])
  )
}

Two analyses per outcome. Pooled correlates every leg’s score change with its outcome change, both arms together. Differential correlates the within-participant differences. BH adjustment runs within each analysis, outcome and collection, never pooled across them.

set_association <- map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
  bind_rows(
    pooled = spearman_by_row(delta, leg_phenotype[[name]]),
    differential = spearman_by_row(paired, paired_outcome[[name]]),
    .id = "analysis"
  ) |>
    mutate(outcome = name)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(analysis, outcome) |>
  left_join(select(catalog, set_id, database, pathway), by = "set_id") |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, "BH"), .by = c(analysis, outcome, database))

Pooling counts a participant’s two legs as independent observations. The check is the median Spearman r between a participant’s BFR and HLRT legs, across sets:

leg_r <- map_dbl(rownames(delta), function(id) {
  cor(delta[id, delta_pairs$BFR], delta[id, delta_pairs$HLRT], method = "spearman")
})
round(median(leg_r), 3)
[1] -0.022

The same correlation inside each arm, untested; it feeds the insets on the pooled figure pages and the set_by_arm sheet.

by_arm <- map(set_names(c("BFR", "HLRT")), function(treatment) {
  keep <- leg_phenotype$treatment == treatment
  map(set_names(outcomes), function(name) {
    spearman_by_row(delta[, keep], leg_phenotype[[name]][keep]) |>
      mutate(outcome = name)
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "treatment")

Compare with chance

With thousands of sets, some reach p < 0.05 by chance. The chance expectation is 5% of the sets tested: the number of nominal hits a collection returns when no set tracks the outcome. The ratio of observed nominal hits to that count reads 1 at chance. Each collection gets its own denominator, so a 41-set collection is not read against a 1,366-set one, and BH runs inside the same split for the same reason.

chance_expectation <- set_association |>
  transmute(
    analysis = paste0("association: ", analysis), comparison = outcome, database,
    n_pairs = n, p, fdr
  ) |>
  summarise(
    features = n(), nominal = sum(p < 0.05), expected = round(n() * 0.05, 1),
    # divide by the exact expectation, not the rounded column above
    ratio = round(nominal / (n() * 0.05), 2), fdr_sig = sum(fdr < 0.05),
    .by = c(analysis, comparison, database, n_pairs)
  )

Rank sets on the protein association

03_Protein_Association saves each protein’s moderated t for the slope of its change on each outcome change, one column per analysis and outcome. fgsea ranks the representative protein of each gene by that t and tests every set, with the sets, size limits and seed of 01_run_fgsea_and_fry and BH over all sets within each ranking. fgsea treats proteins as independent, so a set it calls is a lead; fry, below, is the confirmation, as in 01_.

association_t <- readRDS(here(
  "02_Differential_Expression", "03_Protein_Association", "c_data", "association_t.rds"
))
sets <- readRDS(file.path(gene_sets, "gene_sets.rds"))
gene_of <- read_excel(file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"), "protein_gene_map") |>
  filter(selected)
set.seed(1)
association_fgsea <- map(set_names(colnames(association_t)), function(column) {
  stats <- set_names(association_t[gene_of$protein, column], gene_of$gene)
  fgsea::fgsea(sets, stats, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(leadingEdge = map_chr(leadingEdge, str_flatten, ";"))
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "ranking") |>
  separate_wider_delim(ranking, "_", names = c("analysis", "outcome"), too_many = "merge") |>
  rename(set_id = pathway) |>
  left_join(select(set_catalog, set_id, database), by = "set_id")

fry tests the same slope with the protein correlation kept: for each analysis and outcome it reads the design saved by 03_Protein_Association, refits dpcDE() for that design’s precision weights and asks whether each set moved with the outcome (post:x). Set members become row numbers through each gene’s representative protein, as in 01_.

association_designs <- readRDS(here(
  "02_Differential_Expression", "03_Protein_Association", "c_data", "association_designs.rds"
))
set_rows <- map(sets, function(genes) {
  match(gene_of$protein[match(genes, gene_of$gene)], rownames(proteins))
})
association_fry <- imap(association_designs, function(design, ranking) {
  proteins$weights <- dpcDE(proteins, design, plot = FALSE)$EList$weights
  fry(proteins, set_rows, design, contrast = "post:x", robust = TRUE, sort = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("set_id") |>
    transmute(ranking, set_id, fry_direction = Direction, fry_p = PValue, fry_fdr = FDR)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  separate_wider_delim(ranking, "_", names = c("analysis", "outcome"), too_many = "merge")
association_sets <- left_join(
  association_fgsea, association_fry, by = c("analysis", "outcome", "set_id")
)
association_sets |>
  summarise(fgsea = sum(padj < 0.05), fry = sum(fry_fdr < 0.05), .by = c(analysis, outcome))

Draw figures

figure_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 6.8, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(3, 3, 4, 3)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(4, "mm"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
write_pdf <- function(pages, name) {
  pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", name), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
  walk(pages, print)
  invisible(dev.off())
}

association_figure() draws every set-outcome pair in one collection that reaches nominal p in one analysis, smallest p first, twelve panels to a page; a collection without hits gets no pages. Pooled pages (S11) plot each leg’s score change against its outcome change, with a line fitted inside each arm and the within-arm correlations inset. Differential pages (S12) plot what was tested: one point per participant, the BFR minus HLRT difference in score change against the same difference in outcome change. Each page pools the hits of all four outcomes, so its chance count covers every set-outcome pair in the collection. Pages are built one at a time from their own rows, because a paginating facet would build every panel for every page.

association_figure <- function(which_analysis, number, title, db) {
  hits <- set_association |>
    filter(analysis == which_analysis, database == db, p < 0.05) |>
    arrange(p)
  if (nrow(hits) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  differential <- which_analysis == "differential"
  if (differential) {
    score_change <- paired
    phenotype_change <- paired_outcome
    point_series <- "BFR - HLRT"
    x_label <- "change in set score, T2 - T1, BFR minus HLRT, one point per participant"
    y_label <- "change in phenotype, BFR minus HLRT"
    headroom <- 0.06
  } else {
    score_change <- delta
    phenotype_change <- leg_phenotype
    point_series <- leg_phenotype$treatment
    x_label <- "change in set score, T2 - T1, one point per leg"
    y_label <- "change in phenotype"
    headroom <- 0.35
  }
  points <- pmap(hits, function(set_id, database, pathway, outcome, r, p, fdr, ...) {
    arms <- by_arm |>
      filter(set_id == !!set_id, outcome == !!outcome) |>
      mutate(text = sprintf("%-5s n=%d  r=%+.2f  p=%.3f", treatment, n, r, p))
    label <- paste0(database, ": ", enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000))
    tibble(
      panel = sprintf(
        "%s\nvs %s   r = %+.2f   p %s   q %s",
        str_wrap(label, 40), outcome, r, signif(p, 2), signif(fdr, 2)
      ),
      change = score_change[set_id, ], d_outcome = phenotype_change[[outcome]],
      series = point_series, inset = if (differential) "" else paste(arms$text, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)))
  pages <- unname(split(points, (as.integer(points$panel) - 1) %/% 12))
  imap(pages, function(page, i) {
    page <- droplevels(page)
    page_note <- if (length(pages) > 1) sprintf(" (page %d of %d)", i, length(pages)) else ""
    ggplot(page, aes(change, d_outcome, colour = series, fill = series)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_text(
        data = distinct(page, panel, inset), inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = inset), family = "mono",
        hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.25, size = 1.9, lineheight = 1.2, colour = "grey25"
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, headroom))) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC", `BFR - HLRT` = "grey25"),
        aesthetics = c("colour", "fill"), name = NULL
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 3, nrow = 4, scales = "free") +
      labs(
        x = x_label, y = y_label,
        title = sprintf("S%d. %s, %s%s", number, title, db, page_note)
      ) +
      figure_theme
  })
}

One PDF per collection, so each can be read on its own: S11 for the pooled analysis, S12 for the differential one.

walk(unique(catalog$database), function(db) {
  write_pdf(
    c(
      association_figure("pooled", 11, "Pooled association, all legs", db),
      association_figure("differential", 12, "Differential association, BFR minus HLRT", db)
    ),
    paste0("05_association_", db, ".pdf")
  )
})

S13 is the chance page across all analyses and outcomes: each ratio from chance_expectation drawn as a bar, one panel per analysis and outcome.

chance_plot <- chance_expectation |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(sub("association: ", "", analysis), ", ", comparison)) |>
  ggplot(aes(ratio, database, fill = ratio > 1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%d of %d", nominal, features)),
    hjust = -0.12, size = 2.5, colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "grey72"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
  labs(
    x = "observed nominal hits / chance expectation", y = NULL,
    title = "S13. Nominal hits against chance, by collection and outcome"
  ) +
  figure_theme +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
write_pdf(list(chance_plot), "05_chance_by_collection.pdf")
chance_plot

Save results

05_set_association.xlsx holds chance_expectation (nominal hits against chance), set_association (r, p and BH q per set, analysis and outcome, smallest p first), set_by_arm (the within-arm correlations), association_sets (fgsea and fry on the protein association) and set_catalog (every tested set).

write_xlsx(
  list(
    chance_expectation = chance_expectation,
    set_association = arrange(set_association, p),
    set_by_arm = by_arm,
    association_sets = arrange(association_sets, pval),
    set_catalog = catalog
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "05_set_association.xlsx")
)
